title: Scala
subtitle: Object-oriented and functional programming fused in one statically typed language on the JVM, from a first program to type classes, effects and the tools professionals use.
description: Scala is a statically typed language that first appeared in 2004, created by Martin Odersky and his group at EPFL in Lausanne. It runs on the Java Virtual Machine (and, through Scala.js and Scala Native, in browsers and as native executables), uses any Java library directly, and blends two styles that are often kept apart: every value is an object with methods, and functions are values you pass around and combine. Its type inference keeps code short, while its type system is expressive enough to catch whole classes of mistakes at compile time. Scala is used for back-end services, data engineering (Apache Spark is written in it), financial systems, compilers and research tools.

This course is for anyone who already knows what a variable, a loop and a function are: the Start level of [Lumenary CS](/en/cs/) or equivalent experience in any language. It begins with installing Scala and running a first program with Scala CLI, works through values, functions, case classes, pattern matching, enums and the collections library, and goes on to traits, generics and variance, Scala 3's contextual abstractions (given, using and extension methods), functional error handling with Option, Either and Try, concurrency with Futures, an overview of the effect libraries and Spark, and the build tools of the ecosystem, ending with a complete small project.

To run the code, install Scala from [scala-lang.org/download](https://www.scala-lang.org/download/); since Scala 3.5 the `scala` command is Scala CLI, which compiles and runs a single file with nothing else to set up (you also need a JDK, which the installer can fetch). To try programs in the browser, use [Scastie](https://scastie.scala-lang.org/), the official online playground. Every complete program in these lessons was compiled with Scala 3.10 and run on JDK 21 by Lumenary's test suite, and the output shown is the output it printed. The lessons were drafted with AI assistance and are awaiting review by a human computer scientist.

levels.title: Foundations
levels.summary: Install Scala, run programs with Scala CLI, and learn the core language: values, types and inference, expressions and control flow, and functions and methods.

levels.title: Practice
levels.summary: Model data with case classes and enums and take it apart with pattern matching, transform it with the immutable collections, and abstract with traits, generics, variance, type classes and extension methods.

levels.title: Professional
levels.summary: Handle failure with Option, Either and Try and test it, run work concurrently with Futures, know where Cats Effect, ZIO and Spark fit, use sbt and the rest of the toolchain, and build a complete project in idiomatic style.
